messages:
laura: Quick heads-up — large financial customer asked for an air-gapped POC next month. They want to sideload our product via their jumpbox (no outbound connectivity). Can we provide a signed bundle + a delta patch mechanism? Also asking if we can accelerate security review / SLA exceptions for timeline. cc @mike

mike: We can. Need to confirm two things: 1) max bundle size they can accept (they suggested 15GB), 2) whether they accept GPG-signed artifacts + SBOM. What exact metadata do they need in the manifest?

laura: They said: checksum, signing cert chain, SBOM (CycloneDX ok), and upgrade instructions. Size limit might be negotiable but ops prefers <20GB.

indra: From security: CycloneDX OK. We require: signed SBOM, reproducible build provenance, and attestations for third-party libs. We also need KMS/HSM integration notes for private deployments and details on how secrets are injected in air-gapped installs. No SLA exceptions on security requirements, but we can prioritise review if sales flags it as high priority.

samir: Packaging notes from infra: we can produce two artifact types: full bundle (.tar.gz + .sig) and minibundles (delta patches) generated from our release pipeline. Minibundles are binary diffs; they require the previous bundle version to be present. Recommend tooling: `rdu-delta` (internal) or `bsdiff` for smaller diffs. We sign minibundles as well.

mike: Are minibundles backwards compatible across minor version upgrades? Customer asked about rolling back if patch fails.

samir: Minibundles are only supported for forward updates within the same major version. Rollback path: keep previous full bundle on jumpbox and run rollback script if needed. We'll include `rollback.sh` in bundle and a manifest field `compatible_rollbacks: ["vY-1"]`.

indra: Also want a documented integrity test that customer can run post-install: `sha256sum bundle.tar.gz` + `gpg --verify bundle.tar.gz.sig bundle.tar.gz` and a script to validate SBOM signatures. We'll provide sample commands in the FAQ.

laura: Good. Pricing question: they want an offline license key tied to host fingerprint plus a 90-day trial for the POC. Can we do a time-limited license that avails without internet?

mike: We can issue an offline license blob signed by our License KMS, consumable by the installer. It contains: customer_id, expires_at, allowed_nodes, and fingerprint. It will be validated locally by the agent. For trial, set expires_at to POC end date. Need legal to approve T&Cs for offline trial.

indra: For security, offline license blobs must be revocable. Add revocation list format; customer ops should be able to receive revocation entries during periodic sync windows (they said sync windows are only monthly). Acceptable if revocation is possible via signed CRL file included in periodic minibundles.

laura: Timeline constraints: customer wants initial install week 2 of next month, and then weekly minibundle patches for the 4-week POC. Is weekly delta feasible?

samir: Weekly is fine as long as there are no incompatible schema changes. We'll mark any breaking changes two weeks out and provide both full bundle + minibundle for safety. Also will embargo new quantized weights in minibundles — those go only in full bundles.

mike: Operational ask: what firewall/ports must be opened on their jumpbox to validate signature / license? They prefer zero outbound but will accept occasional outbound to our artifact mirror during a maintenance window.

samir: Installer supports three modes: 1) fully offline (no outbound) using USB/sideloaded artifacts, 2) mirror mode (jumpbox can reach a customer-hosted mirror), 3) proxy mode (jumpbox outbound to our mirror during narrow windows). For fully offline, provide signed artifacts + offline-license. No ports required. For mirror/proxy modes, only HTTPS egress (443) to allowed IPs. We'll provide IP ranges and fingerprint.

indra: Checklist for presales security questionnaire: 1) SBOM (CycloneDX) included, 2) GPG sig + cert chain, 3) reproducible build provenance, 4) KMS/HSM integration notes, 5) revocation/CRL process, 6) audit log export format. I'll draft short answers.

laura: Thanks. Can we ship a proof artifact this week for their ops to validate the sideload flow? They want to test unpack + verify on their jumpbox.

samir: I can export a mini sample bundle (fake runtime, small) — signed, with SBOM and rollback script. Will push to artifact-bot. ETA EOD Thu.

artifact-bot: New artifact uploaded: `sideload-sample-v0.1.tar.gz` — size 9.2MB — sha256: `3f7a2b8c4a9e5f1d6e2c4b7a9d4a8b6c1e3f2a0b9c8d7e6f5a4b3c2d1e0f9a8` — gpg sig at `/artifacts/sideload-sample-v0.1.tar.gz.sig`

mike: Perfect — I'll send the artifact link + install steps to customer ops and request their sandbox test. I'll also open an expedited security review flag with legal for the offline trial terms.

laura: Excellent — I'll update the deal plan and set expectation slides. Thanks team :thumbsup:

indra: I'll start drafting the security questionnaire replies and post the doc in the thread when ready.

samir: One more note — include `manifest.json` with fields: `bundle_version`, `base_version`, `size_bytes`, `signed_by`, `sbom_path`, `minibundle_supported: true`. We'll template it.

laura: Sounds good. If we get a green test from ops this week, Sales will request a 1-week accelerated legal review.

mike: Logged next steps: 1) send artifact, 2) ops test, 3) security doc, 4) legal for offline license. Will follow up after artifact test.

laura: Closing loop — thanks all.
